 Javokhir Sindarov is writing a new page in chess history
 Friday, 13 Nov 2026 
 UTC +1 
 15:30 
 Share this post: 
 CHESS NEWS 
 Tags: 
 FIDE World Championship Match 
 From wunderkind to World Championship challenger, Javokhir Sindarov has enjoyed a remarkable succession of achievements. As he prepares for the greatest challenge of his young career, many experts regard him as the favourite to dethrone the equally young reigning champion. 
 Javokhir Sindarov was born on 8 December 2005 in Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan. He learned the rules of chess at the age of four and soon claimed victory in the Asian School Chess Championship in the under-7 category. His rise continued at an extraordinary pace. He became an International Master in October 2017 and, just one year later, earned the title of Grandmaster.
 At the age of 12 years, 10 months and eight days, he became the second-youngest player in history at the time to achieve this distinction. In the summer of 2019, Sindarov captured the Uzbekistan national championship in emphatic fashion, scoring an impressive 10 points out of 12. He repeated the feat in 2021 and 2024, securing his second and third national titles.
 Photo: Frans Peeters 
 At the beginning of 2021, Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a decree aimed, among other objectives, at establishing Uzbekistan as one of the world’s leading chess nations. The country’s elite players benefited from this ambitious programme of support, and Sindarov eventually committed himself entirely to chess after a brief period of uncertainty about his future.
 His first major breakthrough on the international stage came at the 2021 World Cup in Sochi, Russia. There, he pulled off a stunning upset by eliminating tournament favourite Alireza Firouzja in the second round.
 Photo: Eric Rosen 
 The following summer, Sindarov represented Uzbekistan on board three at the 2022 Chess Olympiad in Chennai. Scoring a solid 6½ points from ten games, he made a valuable contribution to his country’s sensational gold-medal triumph.
 Uzbekistan’s historic victory provided further evidence of the remarkable potential of its young generation and justified the government’s investment in chess development.
 Photo: Lennart Ootes 
 Sindarov continued his steady ascent through the world rankings in 2023, producing strong performances at the World Cup in Baku and the Asian Games in Hangzhou. By the end of the year, he had crossed the coveted 2700-rating threshold, confirming his arrival among the world’s elite.
 After a period of relative stagnation, the defining breakthrough came in 2025. Following a series of impressive performances across several competitions, the almost 20-year-old produced a brilliant performance at the World Cup in Goa, claiming the title and securing his place in the Candidates Tournament.
 Photo: Michal Walusza 
 Held in Cyprus in March and April 2026, the Candidates Tournament brought together eight of the world’s strongest players to determine the challenger for the World Championship. Sindarov made an extraordinary start, winning five of his first six games.
 He never relinquished his grip on the tournament, going on to dominate the competition in a manner unprecedented in the history of the modern eight-player, double-round-robin Candidates format. His triumph earned him the right to challenge reigning World Champion Gukesh Dommaraju at the end of 2026.
 Photo: Niki Riga 
 Sindarov will therefore enter the Salesforce FIDE World Championship Match 2026 with considerable confidence. His recent achievements suggest that he is approaching the contest in excellent form. Most notably, he helped Uzbekistan secure its second Olympic gold medal at the Olympiad in Samarkand last September. Playing on board two, Sindarov scored seven points from ten games and also claimed the individual bronze medal.
 The key to the match will undoubtedly lie in Sindarov’s ability to exploit his principal strengths: an aggressive playing style, exceptional calculation speed and precision, and outstanding tactical acuity. Opening preparation will naturally play a crucial role, particularly as both contenders have demonstrated considerable sophistication and resourcefulness in this area.
 Both players have also shown impressive mental resilience in critical moments, as well as the ability to recover from occasional setbacks in high-pressure competitions. Such qualities could prove decisive in a match where the psychological battle may be every bit as important as the moves played on the board.
 Photo: Michal Walusza 
 This encounter between two of the finest representatives of chess superpowers promises to be a fascinating clash of ambition, talent, and determination. Confidence will undoubtedly be a decisive factor. Sindarov appears to have the psychological advantage on the strength of his recent results, but the balance of power can shift remarkably quickly in a World Championship match. Much may depend on the outcome of the opening games and how each player responds to the inevitable pressure of the occasion.
 Ultimately, the question is an intriguing one: Will Sindarov’s hunger to claim the highest title outweigh Gukesh’s experience of having already conquered the summit of the chess world?
 Written by Yannick Pelletier 
 The Salesforce FIDE World Championship Match 2026 is taking place at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, near Geneva, Switzerland, November 22 to December 12. The first round will be played on November 24. All information on the schedule can be found on the Championship website . Tickets to the playing hall and the fan zone can be bought on the designated website: https://tickets.fide.com/en , while games can be watched on the FIDE YouTube channel.
